semantics.bruteReference: Enumerate each replacement position and candidate v-1,v,v+1 for every original value v, then directly scan modified arrays. Candidates represent every possible integer ordering relative to retained neighbors, including endpoints outside input bounds.
semantics.layout: Two nonempty lines: one n, then exactly n array integers. CRLF accepted without changing source bytes.
semantics.oracle: O(n) strict increasing left/right runs; one-sided extension or join across one replaced element if retained neighbor difference >=2.
semantics.replacement: At most one element of the chosen contiguous segment, to any integer, including 0 or >10^9.
semantics.uniqueOutput: Single exact integer: maximum length. Standard input/output; no interactive, custom, floating, or multiple-valid-output checker.

sourceCorrectionProposal.original: The first line contains integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 105). The next line contains n integers a1, a2, ..., an (1 ≤ ai ≤ 109).
sourceCorrectionProposal.proposed: The first line contains integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10<sup>5</sup>). The next line contains n integers a1, a2, ..., an (1 ≤ ai ≤ 10<sup>9</sup>).

sourceReviewMotivation.finding: Treats at most one non-increasing adjacency as sufficient; no integer bridge feasibility check. The locally reimplemented algorithmic mutant on 4\n1 2 2 3\n predicts 4, whereas exhaustive replacement must give 3. Not a sandbox replay or a qualification kill claim.
